messages: leo: quick pulse on the "empty" capacity card for when min == max. the team flagged a few confusions: label, CTAs, and screen reader copy. maria: saw it. main confusion i've seen in testing: users think min==max means autoscale will never run, but they don't realize it might be intentional (fixed pool). we need language that distinguishes 'locked by policy' vs 'user set'. aj: agree. also: hosted vs dedicated phrasing must be identical. we had a sticky bug where 'Enable burst' appears on dedicated pools that don't support burst. leo: current mock: badge "Fixed capacity" + subtext "Autoscale is off" and a primary button "Enable burst". that was my quick placeholder. priya: engineering note: some pools are marked no-burst in metadata. we should query pool.supportsBurst and show/disable CTA accordingly. prefer disabled button with accessible tooltip over hiding the button. sam: accessibility: when CTA is disabled, screen readers need an explanation. please add an aria-describedby element and include it in the tab order. keyboard users must reach the explanation. maria: copy suggestions: header -> "Capacity locked" (strong). subcopy -> "Min and max are both {N} GPUs. This pool won't grow beyond {N}." primary -> "Enable autoscaling" secondary -> "Edit min/max". leo: i like "Enable autoscaling" instead of 'Allow autoscale'. it's clearer. should cost estimate go next to the primary? example: small muted text: "Est. +$0.12 / hour if autoscaled". aj: yes, include cost but make it optional and opt-in for private installs. add tooltip link to pricing calc. priya: impl: we can compute estimate via the cost service: costEstimate(poolId, 'autoscale'). need privacy ok for private. we should hide the estimate if we don't have permission. sam: visual accessibility: the badge color doesn't pass AA in dark theme at 14px. increase contrast or add an icon+text fallback. also add sr-only summary: "Capacity locked. Autoscaling disabled." maria: guardrail interaction: when SLO slider is set very strict and min==max, show an inline caution: "Selected SLO may require reserving more GPUs. Consider enabling autoscaling or increasing min." with a small link "What this means" to docs. leo: UX flow question: if user clicks "Enable autoscaling", do we immediately open settings or show a confirmation? Product wants minimal modals. Proposal: show an inline confirmation bar: "Enable autoscaling for this pool? This will allow size to vary between {min} and {max2}." Buttons: "Confirm" / "Cancel". aj: inline confirm sounds good. must be implemented as a focus-trapping role=dialog for keyboard+screen reader safety. also show the estimated cost delta in the confirm bar. priya: we already have an inline confirm component in pool-switcher, can reuse. note: when burst unsupported, keep primary button disabled and re-label to "Autoscaling unavailable" with tooltip "Burst not supported on this pool". tooltip must be focusable and dismissible with Esc. sam: add code snippet to the spec showing ARIA attributes: ``` Burst not supported on this pool ``` leo: note for copywriters: avoid verbs like "Allow" or "Permit". use "Enable" or "Turn on". keep microcopy consistent: everywhere we use "autoscaling" or "autoscale"? pick one. i vote "autoscaling" as noun, "enable autoscaling" as CTA. maria: agree. I'll standardize strings in the design tokens doc. also will add a11y acceptance criteria: contrast check, sr-only text, tooltip keyboard support, inline confirm trap. ux-bot: preview built: https://preview.redwood.design/branch/capacity-lock-aria (includes dark mode + keyboard walkthrough). leo: thanks. action items: maria will update Figma and string list, aj to confirm cost display policy for private deployments, priya to wire up supportsBurst flag and reuse confirm component, sam to add accessibility QA steps. i'll update the ticket with final copy and acceptance criteria.
